pages.title: Manage Agents, pools, and scoped secrets
pages.description: Enroll outbound Agents, choose pool semantics, grant secret access, rotate credentials, and inspect health.
pages.intro: Open Runbooks → Agents . Its Agents, Pools, and Secrets tabs separate execution infrastructure from credentials. Agent/pool management requires runbook.agent.manage ; secret administration requires runbook.secret.manage .

sections.heading: Prerequisites
sections.text: - OpsKnight instance reachable over HTTPS from the intended Agent host or network. - Administrative account with runbook.agent.manage and runbook.secret.manage permissions. - Host, Kubernetes cluster, or container engine ready to execute the OpsKnight Agent.

sections.heading: Agent architecture
sections.text: Agents are outbound-only — they poll the control plane for signed work. They do not expose inbound command endpoints. Each Agent: - Generates its own keypair during enrollment (private key never leaves the host). - Verifies the control plane's signature before executing any step. - Signs every API call for mutual authentication. - Reports health, capabilities, and policy hash via heartbeat.

sections.heading: Enroll an Agent
sections.text: Enrollment flow 1. Navigate to Runbooks → Agents and select Add Agent . 2. Enter the Agent name (max 200 chars) and optional hostname hint (max 255 chars). 3. Select Create enrollment . 4. Copy the one-time enrollment token immediately — it expires after 15 minutes and cannot be displayed again. 5. Run the setup instructions on the target host or cluster. 6. Follow the UI setup instructions and pi

sections.heading: Agent authentication protocol
sections.text: Each API call from Agent to control plane is cryptographically signed: Component Description ------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------- Signature algorithm Ed25519/ECDSA PEM Signature window AGENT SIGNATURE WINDOW MS Replay prevention Nonces stored in RunbookAgentRequestNonce table Key storage Agent's private key stays on host; public key stored in databas

sections.heading: Agent status lifecycle
sections.text: Status Meaning Transition ----------- --------------------------------------------- -------------------------------- ENROLLING Token issued, Agent not yet connected Handshake → ONLINE ONLINE Fresh heartbeat within 90 seconds Automatic DEGRADED Heartbeat present but runtime faults reported Automatic OFFLINE Missed heartbeat ( 90s) Computed at query time REVOKED Permanently decommissioned Manual — r

sections.heading: Agent capabilities
sections.text: Agents probe configured binaries and runtime access before heartbeats. The UI distinguishes configured from effective capabilities: Capability Required for ----------------- ------------------------------ Linux diagnostics LINUX DIAGNOSTICS steps Systemd SYSTEMD steps Docker DOCKER steps (runtime: docker) Podman DOCKER steps (runtime: podman) Kubernetes KUBERNETES steps Bash BASH steps Probes are

sections.heading: Create and manage pools
sections.text: In Pools → Create pool , choose semantics explicitly: Mode Behavior Write targeting --------------- -------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------ SHARED TARGET Every healthy member reaches the same target Any eligible member selected LOCAL HOSTS Each Agent represents a different machine Writes require a specific Agent for multi-member pools Poo

sections.heading: Create, grant, and rotate secrets
sections.text: Create a secret In Secrets → Create secret : 1. Enter the name (unique, lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens). 2. Enter the credential value (encrypted at rest, never displayed). 3. Add optional description. 4. Set initial Agent/pool grant. Grant model Secrets are not global — they must be explicitly granted to: - A specific Agent ( agentId ), or - A specific pool ( agentPoolId ). Each grant is unique

sections.heading: Monitor health
sections.text: Runbooks → Health reports queue age, artifact storage, unknown outcomes, expired leases, circuit-breaker indicators, and Agents requiring attention. For detailed health monitoring, see Health and monitoring. For recovery procedures, see Runbook troubleshooting.

sections.heading: Enrollment and policy evidence
sections.text: Setup commands are available only for a verified published server/Agent pair and a confirmed real HTTPS endpoint. Tokens are captured through a hidden prompt or protected file, expire after 15 minutes, and can be revoked by canceling enrollment. Persist each independent Agent's identity and spool volume: - Do not share volumes across simultaneous Agent instances. - Swarm Agents are pinned to the n

sections.heading: See also
sections.text: - Agent operations for deployment prerequisites and topology-specific guidance. - Permissions for all required capabilities. - Health monitoring for fleet-wide health dashboard.

pages.title: Author and publish a Runbook
pages.description: Create workflows with all 9 step types, define typed inputs, configure prechecks and verification, and publish immutable versions.
pages.intro: You need runbook.manage to create or edit drafts and runbook.publish to publish. For Agent-executed steps, arrange an appropriate execution Agent and policy before deployment.

sections.heading: Prerequisites
sections.text: - Active account with runbook.manage permission to create or edit drafts. - runbook.publish permission to release drafts to responders. - For Agent-executed workflows, enrolled and healthy target Agents with appropriate local execution policies. - Familiarity with the risk model.

sections.heading: Create a draft
sections.text: 1. Open Runbooks → Library → New Runbook . 2. Enter a name, unique slug, and optional description. 3. Select a template: - Empty — blank workflow. - Diagnostics — read-only system inspection. - Service recovery — diagnostics + restart + verification (includes approval gate). - Kubernetes recovery — namespace-scoped rollout restart with verification. 4. Create the Runbook. Recovery templates includ

sections.heading: Step types reference
sections.text: OpsKnight supports 9 step types. Each type has a minimum risk floor that the server enforces regardless of the author's label. Control-flow steps (no Agent required) Type Purpose Risk Configuration ----------- ------------------------------------------------------------------ ---------------- ---------------------------------------------------- MANUAL Human instruction — display text for the respo

sections.heading: Configure ordered steps
sections.text: In Builder & Inputs → Builder , select a step from the workflow list. On mobile, select a step to open its full-width editor and use Back to steps to return. For each step, configure: - Name — descriptive name (can use ${{ inputs.key }} templates). - Key — unique identifier within the workflow (lowercase). - Type — one of the 9 step types above. - Action/diagnostic — type-specific action or diagno

sections.heading: Define reusable inputs
sections.text: In Inputs , add typed input definitions that service bindings provide concrete values for: Field Description ----------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Key Unique identifier (lowercase), committed on blur or Enter Label Human-readable display label Type One of: STRING , NUMBER , BOOLEAN , URL , DURATION , SECRET REF , SELECT Required Whether

sections.heading: Prechecks and verification
sections.text: In Configure step , use: - Add precheck under Before action — runs before the main action. - Add verification under After action — runs after the main action. Expand a check to edit it with the same typed controls as a normal step. Use its arrows to reorder or remove it. Read-only, write, and approval badges identify its risk. Check type Behavior ------------ --------------------------------------

sections.heading: Save, publish, and verify
sections.text: 1. Save the draft and wait for Changes saved . 2. Select Validate draft — checks configuration without executing actions. The default step timeout is 600 seconds; the overall deadline defaults to 3600 seconds. Agent claims use a renewable 300-second lease. 3. Select Publish draft , review the confirmation, and confirm. 4. Only the saved draft is published — unsaved editor contents are not included

sections.heading: Version lifecycle
sections.text: State Meaning Editable ----------- ------------------------------------------------------------- -------- DRAFT Work in progress — only one draft per Runbook Yes PUBLISHED Immutable, checksummed version available for service bindings No RETIRED Removed from active use, preserved for audit No Version management operations Operation Required permission Notes ---------------------- ------------------

sections.heading: Compare publication impact
sections.text: Open Compare versions and rule impact before publishing or changing a rule's pin: - Review added/removed/changed actions, derived risk, masked configuration, prechecks, verification, and input changes side by side. - Rules using latest publication track future publications; pinned rules and existing executions retain their frozen versions. - Comparison performs no action and cannot establish platf

sections.heading: Diagnostics and smart targets
sections.text: Use typed Linux DNS, TCP, or HTTP diagnostics for private service checks. Ask the Agent operator to allow the exact hostname and port locally: - HTTP defaults to status 200 and never follows redirects. - Systemd logs or Linux journal provide bounded unit log snapshots. - Container steps select Docker or Podman explicitly. - Kubernetes supports events, rollout status, and scale. Scaling is idempote

sections.heading: Continue with
sections.text: - Service binding and incident response - Agents, pools, and scoped secrets - Action examples - Runbook reference for complete limits and semantics

pages.title: Runbook action examples
pages.description: Configure Kubernetes targets, read-only host checks, HTTP verification, Docker/Podman inspection, and static Bash commands with complete configuration examples.
pages.intro: Follow Author and publish to create and validate each workflow. Start with a manual service binding and Preview execution before executing against a target you are authorized to operate. Preview does not run commands.

sections.heading: Prerequisites
sections.text: 1. Familiarize yourself with the authoring guide, especially step types and risk classes. 2. Ensure you have configured at least one target Agent with appropriate local execution policies. 3. Verify required credentials are configured in Runbooks → Agents → Secrets .

sections.heading: Example 1: Kubernetes recovery with shared target
sections.text: Choose the Kubernetes recovery template. This example declares inputs and uses them across inspection, restart, and verification steps. Input configuration Key Type Example value Description ----------------- ------ ------------- --------------------------- namespace STRING payments Target Kubernetes namespace deployment name STRING checkout Deployment to restart Step configuration Agent requireme

sections.heading: Example 2: Kubernetes scale with input validation
sections.text: Use a NUMBER input for replicas ; the resolved value must be an integer. Scale is idempotent but still a write, subject to approvals and the Agent's kubernetesMaxReplicas policy.

sections.heading: Example 3: Docker or Podman inspection
sections.text: - Keep risk READ ONLY for inspection. - Select an Agent that can reach the exact runtime. - Allow the container through dockerContainers policy (or podmanContainers for Podman). - Runtime socket permissions remain an independent requirement. - Inspection returns bounded output; an absent container fails clearly. For Podman, set "runtime": "podman" and verify the Agent reports the Podman capability

sections.heading: Example 4: Docker health check
sections.text: The health action requires a configured Docker healthcheck reporting healthy . Merely running, starting, unhealthy, or absent healthchecks do not pass this action.

sections.heading: Example 5: Safe systemd checks
sections.text: - Allow the unit through systemdUnits on a host Agent. - A container Agent normally cannot operate the host's systemd without additional configuration. - Logs support 1–500 lines. - Service checks are read-only; restart actions require approval and host permissions.

sections.heading: Example 7: Linux diagnostics workflow
sections.text: Agent-local HTTP checks can reach private services only when both the exact hostname and port are in local networkHosts / networkPorts . Redirects and URL credentials are rejected. DNS uses an allowlisted host and port 53.

sections.heading: Example 8: HTTP verification (control plane)
sections.text: - HTTP steps run on the control plane , using its outbound URL restrictions. - They do not use Agent-local networkHosts policy. - Redirects are rejected; response output is bounded. - A different expected status fails the step. - Place this under After action when it should verify recovery. - HTTP actions do not resolve SECRET REF inputs. Use an Agent executor for secret-backed requests.

sections.heading: Example 9: Static Bash command with input environment
sections.text: Declare STRING input service with value payments-api.service : Agent policy Key points: - Bash steps are classified NON IDEMPOTENT and require approval even when the command only reads state. - Matching is exact — interpolating the command text with ${{ inputs.service }} would change it and break the static allowlist. - Environment variables preserve the command text. - Policy does not grant Unix

sections.heading: Example 10: CONDITION gate
sections.text: A false CONDITION skips itself and all remaining pending workflow steps. It is a workflow gate, not an if/else branch. Incident/service values are read when the condition executes, not frozen at execution creation.

sections.heading: Example 11: WAIT step
sections.text: Duration range: 0–86400 seconds. Subject to the step timeout and overall deadline. Fields named seconds are not WAIT duration controls.

sections.heading: Advanced options
sections.text: The visual editor provides action targets, parameters, safety checks, approval, and step timeout. Use Advanced JSON for: - maxRetries on individual steps. - defaultTimeoutSeconds on the definition (overall deadline). Applying JSON runs the same validation as the visual editor. Unknown outcomes are governed by the engine's retry safety rules; a configured retry count cannot authorize repeating an u

pages.title: Health monitoring and circuit breaker
pages.description: Monitor fleet health, remediation budgets, circuit breaker thresholds, Prometheus alerts, and worker evidence.
pages.intro: Runbooks → Health provides a single dashboard for Runbook system health including fleet status, queue age, artifact storage, unknown outcomes, expired leases, circuit-breaker indicators, and Agents requiring attention.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.text: You need the runbook.read.all capability (see Runbook permissions) to open the health dashboard.

sections.heading: Check Runbook health
sections.text: 1. Open Runbooks → Health and read the overall health ( HEALTHY , DEGRADED , or UNKNOWN ). 2. For each listed issue, match its ID to the issue types below to find the cause. 3. For Agent issues, compare the per-Agent metrics with their thresholds. 4. After fixing the cause, reload the page and verify the issue is gone and the overall health returns to HEALTHY .

sections.heading: Health summary
sections.text: The health dashboard reports: Metric Description --------------------- ------------------------------------------------------ Overall health HEALTHY , DEGRADED , or UNKNOWN Enrolled Agents Total, online, offline, degraded, enrolling, unhealthy Spool depth Pending result uploads queued locally on Agents Dead letter depth Permanently failed/poisoned jobs Oldest pending Age of oldest pending attempt

sections.heading: Health issue types
sections.text: The health page surfaces these specific issue categories: Issue ID Category Trigger condition -------------------- -------- ---------------------------------------------------- worker-evidence Queue Worker status not HEALTHY or redundancy UNCONFIGURED offline-agents Agent Any Agents offline ( 90s no heartbeat) degraded-agents Agent Agents in DEGRADED state enrolling-agents Agent Enrollment tokens

sections.heading: Per-Agent health metrics
sections.text: Each Agent reports: Metric Description Threshold -------------------- ------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------- lastHeartbeatAt Time of last heartbeat 90s → OFFLINE spoolDepth Pending result uploads queued locally High values indicate connectivity issues deadLetterDepth Permanently failed/poisoned jobs Non-zero requires investigation activeAttemptCount Currentl

sections.heading: Circuit breaker
sections.text: The circuit breaker protects against runaway automation: Parameter Value --------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------ Failure threshold 3 failures within 15 minutes Scope Per service Effect Automatic executions halt; transitions to WAITING APPROVAL Recovery Requires human intervention to resume When the circuit breaker trips, automatic rules stop dispatching.

sections.heading: Remediation budgets
sections.text: Administrators configure per-incident limits under Runbooks → Agents → Automatic remediation budgets : Budget Default Maximum Description ----------------------------------- ------- ------- ------------------------------------------------------ Auto executions per incident 3 100 Total automatic workflow starts State writes per incident 3 100 Automatic write actions Non-idempotent actions per incid

sections.heading: Artifact retention
sections.text: Administrators set Execution artifact retention in Runbooks → Agents → Security : Setting Range Default ---------------- ----------- ------------------------------------------------------ Retention period 1–3650 days RUNBOOK ARTIFACT RETENTION DAYS env var (default 30) - Requires admin.manage capability to change. - Background maintenance permanently removes expired artifact contents in bounded ba

sections.heading: Worker health
sections.text: Worker health uses durable PostgreSQL evidence from worker instances and lanes, not the web process's local scheduler state: State Meaning ---------- -------------------------------------------------------------- HEALTHY Fresh successful dispatch and reconciliation within 90 seconds DEGRADED Worker present but reporting faults UNKNOWN Missing or incomplete evidence, even when queue is empty In spl

sections.heading: Prometheus alerting
sections.text: The bundled Prometheus rules include alerts for nonce and artifact maintenance: Stalled maintenance No successful batch in the last 5 minutes (nonces) or 10 minutes (artifacts) while execution workers report healthy. Lagging maintenance Oldest expired data exceeds 5 minutes (nonces) or 1 hour (artifacts), sustained for 5 minutes. Failing maintenance At least 3 failed transactions over 10 minutes,

sections.text: - Troubleshooting for diagnosing specific issues. - Enterprise qualification for load testing and fault receipts. - Agent operations for deployment topologies.

pages.title: Runbook permissions and security
pages.description: All capabilities, API scopes, service authorization, artifact access, and signing key management.
pages.intro: Runbook operations are governed by capabilities (interactive users) and API scopes (machine-to-machine). Service and incident authorization checks apply in addition to these.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.text: Changing who holds a capability is an administrator task; see Manage permissions. Decide which people need to author, publish, execute, or approve Runbooks before you assign capabilities.

sections.heading: UI/interactive capabilities
sections.text: Capability Constant What it allows --------------------------- --------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- runbook.read.all RUNBOOK READ ALL View all Runbooks, executions, Agents, and health runbook.read.scoped RUNBOOK READ SCOPED View only service-scoped Runbooks (reserved for future scoped views) runbook.manage RUNBOOK MANAGE Create/edit/ar

sections.heading: API scopes (machine-to-machine)
sections.text: Scope Purpose --------------------------- ---------------------------------------- runbook-rules:read Read automation rules runbook-rules:write Create/update rules runbook-rules:activate Enable/activate rules runbook-agents:read Read Agent fleet runbook-agents:write Update Agent metadata/labels runbook-agents:enroll Create enrollment tokens runbook-agents:revoke Revoke Agents runbook-agent-pools:w

sections.heading: Service authorization
sections.text: Service rule creation, edits, trigger changes, activation, pause, duplication, detachment, and policy-check requests require both service modification authority and runbook.manage . A service-team responder's read/execute/approve permissions do not grant rule administration. Viewing a service does not grant Runbook library access. The Runbooks view requires runbook.read.all ; other service views d

sections.heading: Artifact access and output security
sections.text: Download controls - Artifact downloads require runbook.artifact.download in addition to Runbook read and resource access. - Downloads are audited and sanitized again, including artifacts stored before this capability was introduced. - The x-content-sha256 header describes the returned sanitized gzip. - Invalid or oversized legacy gzip cannot be downloaded through this endpoint. Output sanitization

sections.heading: Signing key management
sections.text: Execution signing uses a rotation protocol with zero downtime: Phase Status Description ----- -------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------- 1 NEXT staged alongside ACTIVE New key prepared but not yet signing 2 ACTIVE activated, old key → RETIRING New key signs; old key still accepted 3 Old key → RETIRED after 24-hour grace Only new key accepted Distribute the t

sections.heading: Unattended writes authorization
sections.text: Automatic rules that include write steps require separate AUTOMATION PUBLISH capability authorization. This is scoped to a specific unattendedWritesVersionId . Authorization is invalidated if the version, inputs, target, or trigger conditions change (tracked via unattendedWritesScopeHash ).

sections.heading: Verify access
sections.text: After changing a person's role or capabilities, sign in as that person (or ask them to) and confirm that the Runbook actions they need are available and that actions they should not have, such as artifact downloads or publishing, are not.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text: - Manage permissions for the broader authorization model. - Agents, pools, and secrets for infrastructure credentials. - Runbook reference for detailed limits.

pages.title: Bind Runbooks and respond to incidents
pages.description: Select service-specific inputs and targets, configure incident triggers, approve exact plans, and request cancellation.
pages.intro: Publish a Runbook first. You need service modification access and runbook.manage to configure bindings, runbook.execute to start/cancel, and runbook.approve to approve steps. Incident access is checked separately.

sections.heading: Prerequisites
sections.text: - At least one published Runbook workflow available in the library. - Appropriate team or service modification permissions ( runbook.manage ). - Responders executing steps need runbook.execute and runbook.approve permissions.

sections.heading: Attach to a service
sections.text: 1. Open the service's Runbooks tab and choose Attach for the workflow. 2. Select the binding mode: - Manual — responder starts from an incident. Begin here. - Suggested — trigger produces a suggestion; responder decides. - Automatic — trigger starts the workflow (requires pinned version). 3. Select the version strategy: - Latest-published — follows future publications. - Pinned — retains the chose

sections.heading: Configure an incident-created trigger
sections.text: Open Configure on the attached workflow: 1. Set the binding to Suggested or Automatic . 2. In the trigger section, select Incident created . 3. Choose Match all (AND) or Match any (OR). 4. Enter conditions such as Incident urgency Equals HIGH . 5. Save the trigger and check the success message and saved summary. Binding and trigger saves use configuration revisions — if another administrator chang

sections.heading: Service rule checks
sections.text: In Service → Runbooks , create independent rules from published workflows. Each rule type offers different verification: Check What it does Executes actions? -------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------- Validate configuration Checks prospective configuration even while paused No Check Agent policy Sends signed request

sections.heading: Preview and approve
sections.text: Preview execution Open the incident's Runbooks & automation tab and select Preview execution on a suggestion or available workflow: 1. Review the immutable version/checksum, resolved target, redacted inputs, ordered actions, risk, and approval gates. 2. Preview reports current Agent capability and secret-grant checks. 3. Preview creates no execution or queued work. Preview issues a five-minute, si

sections.heading: Execute through the v2 API
sections.text: POST /api/v2/runbooks/{id}/execute uses saved rule inputs when a binding is selected or resolved: - Bound execution — omit parameters or send {} . A non-empty parameters object returns HTTP 400 with RUNBOOK DEFINITION INVALID . - Unbound execution — accepts parameters validated against the published version's input definitions. Supply JSON numbers and booleans with their actual types. Review previ

sections.heading: Cancellation and uncertain outcomes
sections.text: Cancel execution Use Cancel execution and confirm to request cancellation: - Reconciliation handles the request. - Cancellation is not a rollback and does not prove an in-flight write was stopped before executing. - Cancel is a request, not an instant stop — the step may complete before the cancellation is processed. UNKNOWN outcomes For UNKNOWN steps: 1. Independently inspect the target. 2. Recor

sections.heading: Execution timeline and evidence
sections.text: The execution detail page shows: Field Description ------------------------ -------------------------------------- Step/attempt status Current state of each step and attempt Queue time Time spent waiting for dispatch Claim time When an Agent claimed the step Start/completion Execution timestamps Claimed Agent Which Agent executed the step Target Resolved execution target Lease expiry When the Agen

sections.heading: Suggestions and detached rules
sections.text: - Suggestions from detached rules remain visible as historical evidence with Rule detached label. - Preview and execution are disabled for detached suggestions. - Responders with execution permission can still dismiss them. - Paused rules cannot start suggestions until reactivated. - Existing suggestions keep their frozen version, resolved inputs, and target even if the service binding is later ed

sections.heading: Use navigation
sections.text: - Runbooks → Executions for recent execution history. - Runbooks → Health for queue and safety signals. - See troubleshooting for waiting or uncertain executions.

pages.title: Service bindings and triggers
pages.description: Configure automation rules, automatic activation, incident triggers, concurrent edits, and rule lifecycle.
pages.intro: A service automation rule connects a published Runbook to a specific service with concrete input values, an execution target, a binding mode, and optionally an incident-created trigger.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.text: You need service modification authority on the service and the runbook.manage capability (see Runbook permissions), and the Runbook must have a published version to bind.

sections.heading: Rule configuration fields
sections.text: Field Type Description --------------------------- ------- ------------------------------------------------------- name String Optional display name for the rule mode Enum MANUAL , SUGGESTED , or AUTOMATIC enabled Boolean Toggle without deleting versionStrategy Enum PINNED or LATEST PUBLISHED runbookVersionId String? Set when strategy = PINNED defaultAgentId String? Default Agent for executions de

sections.heading: Trigger configuration
sections.text: Supported events Only Incident created ( INCIDENT CREATED ) is wired to runtime evaluation in v2.1. Other enum values ( INCIDENT UPDATED , URGENCY CHANGED , STATUS CHANGED , ALERT RECEIVED , MANUAL , API , CHATOPS , SCHEDULED ) are compatibility identifiers and cannot be configured through the supported trigger schema. Trigger conditions Each trigger supports up to 20 conditions with AND or OR log

sections.heading: Automatic activation
sections.text: Automatic rules always save paused , including configuration changes to an active rule. To activate: 1. Open Rule evidence . 2. Validate configuration. 3. Request fresh Agent policy checks. 4. Use Activate Automatic rule . Requirements: - Each selected Agent must have current successful policy evidence for the frozen version and inputs. - A trigger with no conditions requires explicit confirmation

sections.heading: Concurrent rule changes and pausing
sections.text: Configuration and trigger forms carry the rule revision displayed when the form opened. If another administrator saves, pauses, detaches, or activates the rule first, a stale save is rejected. Reload the page, review the current configuration, and apply your changes again. Pause semantics Operation Behavior -------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------

sections.heading: Rule lifecycle
sections.text: State Description ------------ ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Active Rule is enabled and can dispatch (if conditions met) Paused Rule is disabled; no new triggers fire Detached Archived — disappears from active list; evidence and history preserved Detachment behavior - Historical suggestions retain their rule and trigger identity. - Pending suggestions canno

sections.heading: Service rule pages
sections.text: Service automation lists show 20 rules per page : - Next rules uses a stable creation-time/ID cursor. - First rules returns to the newest page. - Readiness checks and displayed counts apply to the visible page. - Workflow and Agent/pool searches keep inventories bounded.

sections.heading: Context input and target mappings
sections.text: Context input mappings Map Runbook inputs from incident automation context at trigger time: Context target mappings Route execution to a specific Agent/pool based on incident context:

sections.text: State Meaning --------------------- --------------------------------------- PAUSED Rule is disabled BLOCKED Missing requirements prevent activation CHECKS REQUIRED Agent policy checks needed CONFIGURATION VALID Ready for activation UNKNOWN Cannot determine status Online/capable Agents alone cannot produce a target-permission guarantee. Agent policy checks are signed, scoped, one-time results with

pages.title: Service administration tasks
pages.description: Create and operate service ownership, escalation, notification, integration, and lifecycle settings.

Follow Create and manage a service for the full lifecycle. Read Services for data model and authorization semantics. Configure alert context, enrichment, and escalation routing with Configure and roll out service automation, or follow the API authoring w

pages.title: Import and set up business services
pages.description: Create one business service with the guided setup, or many at once from CSV, YAML or a Backstage catalog, with a preview of every change before it is applied.
pages.intro: You need Responder or Admin access. Adding a business service to a status page also needs status page management.

sections.heading: Set up one business service
sections.text: Open Services → Business services → Setup ( /services/business/setup ). Five steps: 1. Name and a short description in your customers' words. 2. Services : tick the technical services behind it. Suggest related services lists the services they depend on, from your active service dependencies; add the ones whose outage would take this business service down too. 3. Ownership : owner team, criticalit

sections.heading: Import many
sections.text: Choose Import on the setup page, pick a format, upload or paste the file, then Preview changes . The preview shows, for each row, whether it is new, changed or unchanged, which fields change, and which services are added or removed. Problems are listed first; while there are any, nothing can be applied. Apply import writes every row in one go, or nothing if something fails, and records one audit e

sections.heading: API
sections.text: - POST /api/v2/business-services/import?dryRun=true with { "format": "csv", "content": "..." } returns the preview; without dryRun it applies. Send an Idempotency-Key . Very large files can exceed the API's transaction time; split them if that happens. - PUT /api/v2/business-services/{id}/supporting with { "businessServiceIds": [...] } sets the business services this one depends on, rejecting loop

pages.title: Business services
pages.description: Group technical services into what customers rely on, follow them in plain language, and see which business services an incident impacts.
pages.intro: A business service is something customers rely on, such as Checkout or Payments , made of the technical services that run it. Its status comes from open incidents , not from the hand-set status of its technical services: a high-urgency incident on Payments API makes Checkout a major outage. Dependencies, supporting business services, maintenance and responder marks count too; Business service heal

sections.heading: Browse the catalog
sections.text: Open Services and select Business services , or press ⌘K and type "business services". Everyone who can see services can open it, including stakeholders. - The header counts business services, how many are impacted now (degraded or worse) and how many sit in each tier. Select a count to filter by it. - Filter by name, health ( Impacted , a single status, or Operational ), tier, owner team, Needs (

sections.heading: Read a business service overview
sections.text: Select a business service to open its overview. The header shows its health and since when, its tier, and four figures: Owner , On call now , Error budget and Open incidents . The header actions are Show on graph , SLA report , a copy-link button and Follow . Responders and Admins also see Edit , which opens the edit form at /services/business/ /edit . When it is impacted, the overview starts with

sections.heading: Create a business service
sections.text: Responders and Admins can create and edit business services. 1. Open Services and select Business services . 2. Select New business service . 3. Give it the name customers use, an optional description, a tier and an owner team you can see. 4. Pick its technical services . Each picker shows the first 50 and searches as you type. A technical service can belong to several business services. You can o

sections.heading: Follow a business service
sections.text: Anyone who can see a business service can Follow it from the catalog or its overview. Followers get a short, plain-language in-app notification when a public incident that impacts it starts, when responders pick it up, and when it is resolved, for example "Checkout is affected" and "Checkout is back to normal". "Impacts" means the same as on the incident: directly, through a dependency or a suppor

sections.text: When a business service's status changes, OpsKnight posts it to: - its Contact channel , when that is a Slack channel (an ID such as C0123ABCD , a name or a channel link) or a Microsoft Teams "Get link to channel" URL; and - the Slack and Teams channels set up on its member services that its owner team owns. Up to 5 channels get each post. Slack or Teams must be connected. When you save a Slack ch

sections.heading: Status page updates
sections.text: When a business service becomes impacted, or recovers, OpsKnight writes an update on every enabled status page that shows it, using the name the page shows. By default it is a draft : an admin reviews it under the page's announcements ( Drafts ) and publishes it as usual. When it recovers, an impact draft nobody published is removed. With automatic publishing on, the published impact update also e

sections.heading: Error budget alerts
sections.text: Admins can turn on Alert on error budget changes in Settings → Notifications , under Monthly service reviews , then Save . It is off by default. Every 15 minutes OpsKnight checks each business service with an SLO target. When its budget turns at risk or is exhausted, it tells the owner, the owner team and followers in-app, by email and in the business service's Slack or Teams channels. A recovery

sections.text: Both are in Settings → Notifications and only admins can change them. - Ownership reminders , next to the service review settings, notify owners at most once a week per issue when a review is overdue, the owner is inactive or the owning team has no one on call. Off by default. - Business service scorecards set the rules every business service is scored against, grouped into levels. A level is reac

sections.heading: Who sees what

Hover a chip for the reason (its service is affected, a service it depends on is affected, a business service it relies on is affected, or marked by a responder); select it to open the business service. Responders can correct the list on desktop: + Impacted business se

pages.title: Schedule service maintenance windows
pages.description: Hold new alerts for one or more services during planned work, repeat windows on a schedule, and decide what happens to held alerts when the window ends.
pages.intro: New in 2.2.0. A maintenance window tells OpsKnight that planned work is under way on one or more services, so alerts that the work causes do not page anyone.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.text: - You need permission to change every service the window covers (the same permission as editing the service). - Know the start time, the expected duration, and which services the work touches. - If customers should see the work, have a status page that shows those services.

sections.heading: Open the feature
sections.text: Open Services , select a service, and choose the Maintenance tab. Services in an active window show an In maintenance badge in the service list and on the service page.

sections.heading: Configure a window
sections.text: 1. Select Schedule maintenance . 2. Enter a Title and, optionally, a Description . 3. Under Repeat , keep Does not repeat for one-off work, or choose Daily , Weekly (pick the days), or Monthly (pick the day; it is moved to the last day of shorter months). Set how often it repeats, the start date and time, the Time zone , and an optional end date. 4. For one-off work, choose Start now or a start ti

sections.heading: How a maintenance window works
sections.text: - While a window is active, a new alert for a covered service opens a Suppressed incident linked to the window. Nobody is paged, the SLA clock is paused, and Runbooks are not started. - Incidents that were already open keep escalating. Incidents a person creates by hand are never held. A resolve event from the source still closes a held incident. - Held incidents are hidden from the default incide

sections.heading: Verify the result
sections.text: 1. Confirm the service shows In maintenance during the window. 2. Send a test event to the service's integration and confirm it creates a Suppressed incident that does not page the on-call responder. 3. After the window ends, confirm the held incident was released or resolved as you chose.

sections.heading: Change or undo it
sections.text: - End now ends an active window early. It asks for confirmation, because paging resumes. - Delete removes an upcoming window. A window that holds incidents cannot be deleted; end it instead. - Recurring schedules can be edited, paused, resumed, or deleted from the Maintenance tab.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - An alert still paged during maintenance: the incident was already open before the window started, was created by a person, or belongs to a service the window does not cover. - Held incidents were not released at the end: open Settings → System → Health . The Maintenance windows check reports windows that ended but were not processed, which usually means the scheduler role is not running. - You c

pages.title: Create and manage a service
pages.description: Create a service, assign ownership and response settings, verify integrations, and safely retire it.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.text: Identify the service owner/team, escalation policy, notification destinations, integration sources, and retirement requirements. You need service-management permission.

sections.heading: Open the feature
sections.text: Open Services . Select an existing service or choose Create service .

sections.heading: Configure the service
sections.text: 1. Enter a unique, recognizable name and useful description. 2. Assign the responsible team and verify membership/lead coverage. 3. Attach the tested escalation policy and verify its steps target the intended on-call schedule. A service does not attach a schedule directly. 4. Open Notifications and configure provider destinations and routing. 5. Open Integrations or Webhooks and add only sources t

sections.heading: How service ownership works
sections.text: Service scope controls incident routing and is reused by reports, dashboards, integrations, teams, and status communication. Changing its team or policy affects future routing; it does not rewrite historical incident ownership.

sections.heading: Service intelligence
sections.text: Users with the intelligence.read permission see an Intelligence tab on the service page (shareable as /services/ /intelligence ). It shows SLO burn, dependencies, alert quality, recent changes, noise controls, recurring problems, grouping mode and learned facts for that service. Responders do not see the tab while both alert grouping and noise control are off for the service; users who can manage

sections.heading: Verify the service
sections.text: Send a controlled test alert. Confirm it creates or updates the expected incident, selects the intended policy/on-call responder, reaches every intended destination once, and is visible to the correct team.

sections.heading: Remove or retire a service
sections.text: Stop inbound sources first, remove destinations/secrets, preserve required incident and audit history, and reassign dependent objects. Delete only after dependency warnings are resolved and retention policy permits it.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - Wrong responder: inspect attached policy, schedule coverage, and overrides. - No notification: separate ingestion, routing, queue, provider, and destination state. - Test creates duplicates: verify integration deduplication key and service mapping. - Cannot edit/delete: confirm permission, ownership, and dependent objects.

sections.heading: Next steps
sections.text: - Manage a team - Configure escalation - Configure notification routing

pages.title: Author and operate automation through the API

pages.intro: This walkthrough implements the same example as the UI guide. Use a test service first.

sections.text: This walkthrough requires an administrator-owned API key with automation:read , automation:write , and automation:publish ; reading incident decisions also needs incidents:read . A responder with write scope can prepare an owning-team draft but cannot publish or enable Live. Use Bearer API authentication. Set OPSKNIGHT URL , OPSKNIGHT SERVICE ID , and OPSKNIGHT API KEY in your client session. Obta

sections.heading: 2. Prepare the complete snapshot

sections.text: POST the same automation-draft.json body to /api/v2/services/{id}/automation/validate . Review both blocking errors and warnings. For /simulate , use a body containing the same snapshot , an event from the UI example, integrationType , and optional service-owned integrationId , providerPayload , and ISO evaluationAt . Use the integration's actual type; built-in integration conditions and type-rest

sections.heading: 4. Publish and enable Shadow
sections.text: POST /api/v2/services/{id}/automation/publish with the updated draft ETag, a fresh idempotency key, and this body for a service with no active version: For an existing service, supply its actual active version ID. While Live, include expectedCandidateVersionId as well; an existing candidate cannot be replaced without its expected identity. Publication returns immutable version identity, not an ETa

sections.heading: 5. Verify ingestion and enable Live
sections.text: Send representative alerts through the service's configured integration, using unique deduplication keys. Query /automation for effective mode and health and /automation/decisions for incident-scoped decisions. Read /automation/observations for discovery metadata; the public API does not return raw previews or hashes. Use cursor pagination for bounded lists. Once reviewed, GET configuration again

sections.heading: 6. Publish and promote a candidate
sections.text: Save and publish a changed draft while Live. The response identifies the candidate; the existing active version continues routing. GET /automation/candidate for its snapshot, comparison aggregates, readiness policy/results, and pending-work sample. After reviewing evidence, POST /automation/candidates/activate with a fresh idempotency key and: Replace the policy revision with readiness.settingsRev

sections.text: GET /automation/versions and /automation/versions/{versionId} to review history. POST /automation/restore with { "sourceVersionId": "REPLACE WITH VERSION ID" } , the current draft ETag , and a fresh idempotency key. Restore only creates an editable draft; publish and, when Live, promote the resulting candidate explicitly. PATCH mode to DISABLED with the current configuration ETag and active versio

pages.title: Service automation examples and starter templates

sections.heading: Prerequisites
sections.text: Complete the initial setup and rollout, prepare sanitized samples, and identify the active escalation policies and service-owned channel destinations you intend to use. The recipes below describe configurations to create in Context and Rules; they are not ready-made provider payload contracts. 1. Choose a recipe and confirm the actual EVENT or PROVIDER extraction path. 2. Create its fields with ca

sections.heading: Use a starter template deliberately
sections.text: Starter templates prepare a draft; they do not publish or enable automation. Their default route is Use service default . Select a different policy or add channel actions yourself if that is the desired outcome. The starter templates cover: - Route by alert priority : a routing condition on built-in priority in P1/P2. - Route production alerts and Route by environment : an environment choice field

sections.heading: Route an enterprise customer to a dedicated policy
sections.text: Create a text field customer tier , case-insensitive, with a mapping to the actual provider path. For the starter's sample, the provider payload is: Add a routing rule with customer tier EQ enterprise , selecting the intended escalation policy. Put it before a final service-default route. Add a Slack or Teams notification to that same rule if the dedicated channel also needs the alert. Verify Ente

sections.heading: Route a particular AWS account
sections.text: Keep aws account as text. Account identifiers are identifiers, not quantities; using a number type changes comparison behavior and can discard leading zeroes. Map PROVIDER AWSAccountId only if that is the actual provider's path; other AWS integrations can use different envelopes. Discovery excludes phone-shaped values, which can also exclude a numeric account identifier. Use the known sender schem

sections.heading: Enrich numeric and boolean context
sections.text: For a numeric example, declare NUMBER error rate mapped from EVENT payload.custom details.error rate . An enrichment rule with error rate GTE 5 can set P1 and add a high-error-rate tag. This example assumes your sender reports percentage units: 5 means 5%, not a fraction of one. Test numeric 5 , numeric string "5" , a lower value, missing data, and "unknown" . Numbers and numeric strings normalize

sections.heading: Add channel notification without suppressing responder escalation
sections.text: Create a routing rule with one responder action and one or more supplemental channel actions. For example, a production match can use a named escalation policy and notify the enabled service-owned Slack destination. Select destination identities from the service configuration; a channel name or webhook URL is not a destination ID. A destination from another service or a disabled destination fails

sections.heading: Pass context to a Runbook safely
sections.text: Use a successful Live automation evaluation to capture fields such as environment for a service Runbook binding. The binding references automation.environment using its own condition editor and operator names. Input and approved-target mappings instead use the unprefixed contextKey value environment ; do not use the condition field name as a mapping key. Runbook conditions are a separate contract:

sections.heading: Verify before adopting a recipe
sections.text: Confirm the exact version, normalization state, matching rule, final priority, responder route, and any intended channel delivery. Test missing/unmapped fields, overlapping routes, unexpected types, and a provider sample that differs from the normalized event. Then follow the candidate rollout for later changes.

pages.title: Configure and roll out service automation
pages.description: Build context fields and rules, test alerts, publish safely, review Shadow results, and recover from routing mistakes.
pages.intro: Use this guide to introduce alert enrichment and routing on one service, then change it safely while Live. Read the concept first if you are unfamiliar with context fields or Shadow mode.

sections.heading: Prerequisites
sections.text: - A service with a known owner, a working inbound integration, and an intentional default escalation policy. - An administrator for global settings, publication, and mode changes. A responder on the owning team can prepare the draft. - Representative sanitized alerts, including missing and unexpected values. - Working background workers for observation aggregates and supplemental delivery. - Enabl

sections.text: 1. Open Services , select the service, and open Automation . 2. Inspect Overview for the current mode, published version, health, and configuration problems. 3. Have an administrator enable Enable service automation globally in system settings. Leave the service Disabled while authoring. 4. Use Context , Rules , and Test to prepare the draft. Activity holds published history and restoration contro

sections.text: This example routes production alerts normally and suppresses responder escalation only for explicitly recognized staging and development alerts. 1. In Context , create a choice field with key environment and label Environment . 2. Add canonical choices production , staging , and development . 3. Keep matching case-insensitive. Add aliases prod and prd → production , and stg → staging . 4. For an

sections.text: In Rules , add these rules: 1. An enrichment rule named Production priority : when environment equals production , set priority to P1 and add tag production . 2. A routing rule named Known non-production : when environment is in [staging, development] , select No escalation . 3. A final routing rule named Default response : no conditions, use the service default escalation policy. For a separate p

sections.heading: 4. Test the draft without sending notifications
sections.text: In Test , select the intended integration context and use a sanitized normalized event such as: Supply the provider payload separately when testing PROVIDER mappings. Running a sample evaluates the current draft without creating incidents or notifications. Inspect extraction, condition results, enrichment, and the selected route. Repeat these cases and confirm the expected results: - prd : recogni

sections.text: 1. Save the draft and resolve blocking validation issues. 2. Review the publication diff, policy references, and channel destinations. 3. Have an administrator publish the version. Record its number. 4. Set the service to Shadow . 5. Send representative alerts through the real integration. Use unique deduplication keys so each creates a new test incident. 6. Review Overview , recent evaluations, a

sections.heading: 6. Enable Live
sections.text: Have an administrator review the published version and switch to Live . Every mode change to Live checks dependencies and asks for explicit acknowledgement if that version has no recent Shadow evaluations or recorded errors/fallbacks. These checks also apply when re-enabling a previously Live service after Disabled or Shadow. The candidate readiness thresholds below are a separate promotion contra

Allow new traffic to evaluate the candidate in Shadow against actual Live results. 4. Review routing, priority, and suppression differences and any fallback/error counts. 5. Review candidate readiness. Defaults require at least 100 evaluations in the seven

sections.text: For one service, select Disabled to stop evaluating automation for newly accepted work. Already accepted work may carry its original mode/version pointers; use the global switch for an emergency stop that also fences enabled backlog. For a global incident, save global OFF in system settings. This resets service modes to Disabled. Re-enabling global automation requires deliberate service-by-service

Mark an intentionally unused field as Display only to avoid the unused-field warning. This flag does not disable extract

pages.title: Service graph

pages.intro: Services → Service graph ( /services/graph ) draws your business services and technical services, and how they depend on each other, with live health. Use it to answer "what does Checkout rely on?" and "what else breaks if Payments API is down?".

sections.heading: Read the graph
sections.text: - Business services are square-cornered cards; technical services are rounded. Each card shows the name, the team, a status badge and the number of open incidents. Business service cards also show their tier and how many services they contain; Tier 0 cards have a heavier frame. The coloured left edge repeats the status: emerald operational, amber degraded or partial outage, crimson major outage, b

The address then carries ?focus=bs: (business service) or ?focus=svc: (technical service), and the graph shows only that service and everything within two dependency steps , at most 500 services. Remove the Focus chip to see the whole graph. Without a focus the graph shows every serv

The list is the keyboard and screen-reader alternative to the canvas; its rows

Only technical services connect. - Remove: click a solid dependency line to see its details (type, origin, traffic, confidence, criticality, evidence and note), then Remove… and confirm. A d

Ticks under the slider mark days when incidents were opened and dependencies changed. A banner shows the time you are looking at; Back to now returns to the live graph. Dependencies, incidents and statuses are replayed; membership, maintenance windows and

sections.text: Export downloads JSON (loaded graph) or SVG (current layout) . The SVG uses your current light or dark theme and the positions on screen.

sections.text: Anyone who can read services can open the graph. It only ever shows services, business services and incidents you can access; a dependency that touches a hidden service is left out and never walked through in focus mode. Suggested dependencies appear only for roles that can read intelligence suggestions. Stakeholders see open-incident counts but not the incidents.

sections.text: GET /api/v2/business-services/{id}/graph?hops=1..3 returns the same graph around one business service ( services:read ), and the MCP tool business service graph exposes it to assistants. See the API reference.

pages.title: Alert on SLO burn rate
pages.description: Page or open a ticket-urgency incident when an availability objective spends its error budget too fast, measured from good and total event counts in your metrics backend.
pages.intro: New in 2.3.0. A burn-rate alert watches one availability or uptime objective and raises an incident when the error budget is being spent much faster than the objective allows. It measures real traffic: two queries against a metrics connection count the good events and the total events in each 5-minute step. Burn-rate alerts are off until you enable them, per objective.

sections.heading: How it decides
sections.text: Burn is how fast the budget is spent: (1 − good ÷ total) ÷ (1 − target) . At 1× the budget lasts exactly the objective's window; at 14.4× a 30-day budget is gone in about two days. Each tier checks a long window and a short window. It fires only when both burn at or above its threshold, so an outage that has already stopped does not keep alerting. Tier Long window Short window Threshold Incident s

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.text: - You need administrator access. - The objective must belong to a service and measure Uptime or Availability . - An enabled metrics connection (Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog or CloudWatch) that the service's team may use. See observability connections. - Intelligence must be enabled: policies are evaluated by the intelligence lane, every 5 minutes.

sections.heading: Set up the alert
sections.text: 1. Go to Settings → Service objectives , find the objective and choose Edit . 2. Open the Alerting tab. 3. Choose the Metrics connection . 4. Enter the Good events query and the Total events query . Each must return a count of events per 5-minute step in the connection's own language. Every series a query returns is added up. For Prometheus: 5. Choose Test queries . OpsKnight runs both queries ove

sections.heading: Watch it
sections.text: Open the service and choose Intelligence . In SLO burn , each objective with a policy shows its alert state ( Alerting: OK , Alerting: ticket , Alerting: paging or Alerting off ). Enabled policies also show the last day as a chart: the SLI per step, the burn over the trailing hour, the tier thresholds as dashed lines, and the alert transitions underneath. Choose Table for the same values as text.

sections.heading: API and MCP
sections.text: - GET /api/v2/service-objectives/{id}/alert-policy : the policy and its current state (404 without one). - PUT /api/v2/service-objectives/{id}/alert-policy : create or replace the policy. Needs service-objectives:write and an Idempotency-Key ; enabled defaults to false . - GET /api/v2/service-objectives/{id}/burn-history?hours=24 : stored steps (up to 168 hours), transitions and tier thresholds. sections.text: The policy's last status explains the latest evaluation: Status Meaning -------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------- OK Evaluated normally. NO DATA The queries returned no steps with a total. CONNECTOR ERROR: The connection failed (for example TIMEOUT ); the state is unchanged. CONNECTION DISABLED Enable the connection again. CONNECTION NOT ALLO

pages.title: Keep stakeholders informed

pages.intro: Support leads, account managers and executives need to know when Checkout is down, not which pod restarted. OpsKnight gives them the Stakeholder role, subscriptions to business services, and updates you send from the incident.

They cannot: - open incidents, incident lists or anyth

Team members who turned off team notifications are skipped; - were added by Subscribe all users , which makes everyone active today a follower. People who join later are not added, and anyone can unfollow. Set teams and "subscribe all" in the setup wizard.

sections.text: On the incident, next to Impacts , choose Notify stakeholders : 1. Pick the stage: Investigating, Identified, Monitoring or Resolved. A message template with the business service names fills in. 2. Edit the message in plain language. Say what customers notice and when the next update is. 3. Send update . Followers and subscribed team members of the impacted business services get an email and an in

It shows only what is safe to share: each business service's status, how long it has had it, and counts. It never shows inciden

Each tile shows the st

Open Status dashboard and select Manage dashboards . 2. Select New dashboard , give it a name and a URL ( /status-dashboard/ ), and pick its business services. 3. Select Create dashboard . The board opens; share its link. Custom dashboards appear as tabs above th

sections.text: /m/status in the mobile app lists the same business services, worst first, with their status and since when.

sections.text: If the board says Health is unavailable right now , live status could not be loaded. It tries again on its next refresh, every 30 seconds.

pages.title: Status-page operations
pages.description: Configure the single status page, publish updates, and manage subscribers and API access.
pages.intro: OpsKnight 2.0 supports one status page per deployment. Start with Create and configure, validate its public origin and components, then practice publishing an incident update. pages.intro: A status page can list its services in three ways. Choose one in Settings → Status pages → your page → Services → Layout . Layout What visitors see -------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Technical services One row per technical service, exactly as before. Business services

sections.heading: How status, history and uptime are worked out
sections.text: - Status is the worst current status of the business service's services on this page. - History shows, for every moment in the last 90 days, the worst status of any of them. - Uptime is the uptime of its least available service; incident counts are added up. Only services published on this page count. Hide a technical service under its business service in the editor to keep it out of the business

sections.text: 1. Create business services first. 2. In Services → Layout , pick Business services or Business services, expandable . 3. Add business services: type in Find a business service to add to narrow the list, then click one. Their technical services are added to the page automatically. 4. Order them by dragging or with the arrows. A business service that supports another one on the page is indented und

sections.text: Each business service on the page has its own settings, saved with the page: - Name on page : what visitors see, for example "Buying things" instead of "Checkout". - Show on page : off keeps it off the page. Updates that name it still count its services. - List its services : off keeps the row closed even on the expandable layout, so visitors see the business service but not its parts. - Order : d

sections.heading: Pin a status (override)
sections.text: Sometimes the computed status is not what customers experience, for example during a partial rollback. Click Override status next to a saved business service, pick a Public status and Apply now . A business service you just added needs a page save first. The page shows that status instead of the computed one until the end time you choose (blank means 30 days, the maximum). Automatic (from incident

sections.text: An affected business service shows when the problem started, for example "Partial outage since 22 Nov, 10:04", in the page's time zone. On a live page a row that becomes affected opens again even if the visitor closed it.

sections.heading: Updates that name business services
sections.text: When you write an incident update or an announcement, tick Affected business services to name them instead of each technical service. Every service inside counts as affected: - a maintenance that names a business service puts its services in maintenance on the page; - the update card lists the business services, and the services and regions inside them; - subscribers to those business services or

sections.heading: Subscribers
sections.text: On a grouped page the subscribe form offers business services, plus any services outside them. A subscriber who picks Checkout hears about incidents and announcements on any of Checkout's services. People who pick nothing still get every update.

sections.heading: Themes, mobile and accessibility
sections.text: The layouts use the page's theme colours, so every built-in theme and custom CSS keep working, in light and dark. Expandable rows are buttons that announce whether they are open, work with the keyboard and have 44px touch targets on phones.

sections.heading: API
sections.text: GET /api/v2/status-pages/{id}/business-services returns the layout and business services. pages.title: Create and configure the status page
pages.description: Configure the single supported status page, services, routing, access, and publication state.
pages.intro: OpsKnight 2.0 supports one status page. The control center may use plural route names, but it deliberately disables additional creation after the first page exists.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.text: List customer-facing services, choose a stable slug/domain, decide public versus authenticated access, and prepare branding/contact ownership. You need administrator access.

sections.heading: Open the feature
sections.text: Open Settings → Status Pages . If no page exists, select Create Status Page ; otherwise open the existing page workspace.

sections.heading: Configure the page
sections.text: 1. Create the page in draft/disabled state with a clear public name and unique slug. 2. Map services, set their order, and enable Show on page only for customer-relevant services. 3. Configure branding, organization/contact details, allowed incident fields, and privacy mode. 4. Choose public access or Require authentication . Test restricted access in a signed-out browser. 5. Configure the default

sections.heading: What OpsKnight does
sections.text: The page workspace builds a public/preview snapshot from mapped services, incidents, announcements, privacy policy, and routing configuration. Disabled pages remain administrative drafts. Default routing, slug, subdomain, and custom domain are distinct resolution paths.

sections.heading: Verify the page
sections.text: Open the exact public URL in a private browser. Confirm access behavior, branding, service order/status, announcement visibility, and absence of private fields. Trigger and resolve a synthetic incident and verify the projected update.

sections.heading: Change or undo
sections.text: Disable the page before risky routing/privacy changes. Preserve the old domain until the new route is verified. Removing a service hides future projection but does not erase historical operational records.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - Cannot create another page: one page is supported in 2.0; configure the existing page. - Page unavailable: confirm enabled state, route resolution, DNS/TLS, and access mode. - Service missing: map it and enable Show on page . - Private data visible: disable the page, correct allowed fields/privacy, rebuild snapshot, and retest signed out.

sections.heading: Next steps

pages.title: Publish a status update

sections.heading: Before you begin

Identify the customer-facing impact, approved wording, affected services/components, intended component state, privacy settings, and person authorized to publish. Internal incident visibility does not automatically define public output.

sections.heading: Open the feature
sections.text: Open Settings → Status page to review the single installation-wide page and service/component mapping. During response, open the incident's status communication controls.

sections.heading: Configure the update
sections.text: 1. Confirm the affected internal services are mapped to the intended public components. 2. Select the incident/component state that accurately describes customer impact. 3. Write a concise customer-safe title and update: impact, start/current state, mitigation or next action, and next-update expectation. 4. Review whether title, description, assignee, urgency, custom fields, timestamps, and histor

sections.heading: What OpsKnight does
sections.text: OpsKnight projects deliberately selected incident/service state into one supported status page. The projection layer controls public fields; it does not serialize the internal incident directly. Subscriber and webhook delivery are asynchronous and separate from page rendering. Drafts from open incidents When the intelligence master switch and Show small helpers are on (both off by default), the st

sections.heading: Verify it worked
sections.text: Open the public or authenticated page through the same hostname/audience customers use, preferably in a signed-out/private browser. Confirm component state, wording, timestamps/history, privacy, and mobile layout. Inspect subscriber/webhook delivery separately and allow for documented cache/custom-domain delay.

sections.heading: Change or undo the update
sections.text: Publish a correcting/follow-up update rather than rewriting history silently. When service health is restored, publish the resolution/normal component state and verify the public page plus subscriber projections. Unmap a service only after confirming it should no longer appear; OpsKnight 2.0 supports one status page, not a second replacement page.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: Internal incident changed but page did not: verify deliberate publication/projection state, service mapping, projector heartbeat/backlog, and current incident generation. Wrong information is public: publish a correction immediately, tighten privacy/projection settings, and review the exposure/audit trail. Custom domain is stale/unreachable: compare canonical page, DNS/TLS, proxy/cache, and config

pages.title: Team administration tasks

pages.title: Create and manage a team
pages.description: Create a team, manage members and service ownership, offboard responders, and delete safely.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.text: Identify the team owner/lead, responders, services, on-call participation, and whether SCIM or OpsKnight owns membership.

sections.heading: Open the feature
sections.text: Open Teams , select a team, or choose the create action.

sections.heading: Configure the team
sections.text: 1. Enter a unique team name and operational description. 2. Add intended members and confirm each user is active. 3. Set supported team leadership/ownership fields. 4. Assign services and verify the team can read and operate them. 5. Confirm members appear in on-call, notification, and collaboration selectors where their roles permit it. 6. Save and reload the team detail.

sections.heading: How membership works
sections.text: Team membership scopes service access and ownership but does not itself grant an administrator or responder system role. When SCIM Groups own membership, change the provider assignment and let provisioning reconcile it.

sections.heading: Verify the team
sections.text: Sign in as a representative member and confirm intended services are visible, unowned services remain inaccessible, and notification/on-call participation is correct.

sections.heading: Remove members or delete the team

Before deleting a team, reassign services, incidents, escalation targets, dashboards, and integrations. SCIM group DELETE can also delete the mapped team; review that policy first. OpsKnight refuses to delete a team that still has unresolved incidents or is a target in an escalation policy st

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - Member cannot see a service: verify both team assignment and system role. - Member returns after removal: SCIM is likely authoritative. - Delete is unsafe or blocked: inventory and reassign dependent objects. - On-call is wrong: membership alone does not place a user in a rotation.

pages.title: Amazon CloudWatch
pages.description: Connect Amazon CloudWatch alerts to OpsKnight incident ingestion.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.text: The Amazon CloudWatch adapter accepts inbound webhook events at /api/integrations/cloudwatch , validates them through its custom handler, normalizes provider payloads, and submits lifecycle events to the configured service.

sections.heading: Prerequisites
sections.text: - An OpsKnight service and enabled integration record. - Permission to create or use an Amazon SNS topic and change CloudWatch alarm actions. - The exact SNS topic ARN in the same AWS partition/region used for the alarm action. - A network path from the provider to the OpsKnight web runtime.

sections.heading: Setup and configuration
sections.text: 1. In Amazon SNS → Topics , create or select a Standard topic dedicated to the intended OpsKnight service/environment. Copy its full topic ARN. 2. In OpsKnight, open Services → select service → Integrations → Add integration → Amazon CloudWatch . 3. Enter the exact SNS Topic ARN , save, and copy the generated HTTPS endpoint containing integrationId . 4. In Amazon SNS → Subscriptions → Create subsc

sections.heading: Authentication and request verification
sections.text: The endpoint requires the integration identifier. Signature verification is none using the cloudwatch verification contract. The exact payload schema is defined by src/app/api/integrations/cloudwatch/route.ts and src/lib/integrations/cloudwatch.ts . - Method: POST - Integration identifier: query parameter - Integration key transports: none; this route uses the authentication contract above - Schem

sections.heading: Event mapping and incident lifecycle
sections.text: The adapter emits the lifecycle actions found in its current source: - trigger - resolve Correlation contract: adapter EventPayload.dedup key . Recovery contract: adapter emits resolve for its recovery state .

sections.heading: Recovery and deduplication
sections.text: This route has no provider delivery-ID fence; incident convergence relies on the adapter deduplication key. Incident convergence still depends on the adapter correlation key. Failed deliveries are recorded for operational inspection without exposing secrets.

sections.heading: Limits and testing
sections.text: Per-integration rate limiting protects the ingestion path. Send a representative trigger and recovery pair in a non-production service, verify that one incident is created, and confirm that recovery updates that incident rather than creating another.

sections.heading: Verify the connection
sections.text: After the test alert, confirm all of the following: - One incident appears for the selected OpsKnight service. - The incident source identifies Amazon CloudWatch. - A repeat event updates or correlates according to the adapter identity. - A recovery event resolves the correlated incident.

sections.heading: Error reference
sections.text: - 400 — Invalid request or payload validation failed. - 401 — Configured authentication or signature validation failed. - 403 — Integration is disabled. - 404 — Integration record was not found. - 413 — Payload exceeds the one MiB body limit. - 429 — Per-integration request rate exceeded. - 500 — Provider event processing failed.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: 1. Confirm the integration is enabled, belongs to the intended service, and stores the exact topic ARN. 2. In SNS, confirm the HTTPS subscription is Confirmed , not PendingConfirmation , and its endpoint contains the correct integration ID. 3. Inspect the webhook HTTP response body and system logs for schema, topic-binding, certificate URL, or SNS signature errors. 4. Check SNS delivery status/log

sections.text: Use HTTPS, rotate exposed keys at both systems, configure signature verification when supported, and restrict provider egress or ingress controls without blocking legitimate retries.

pages.title: Disconnect or reconnect Microsoft Teams
pages.description: Rotate or replace Teams tenant and Bot credentials while safely revalidating installations, destinations, cards, actions, and war rooms.

sections.heading: Before you begin

sections.text: 1. Record affected resource identities without credentials. 2. Update or disconnect OpsKnight configuration. 3. Update Azure Bot/Entra and generated Teams package as required. 4. sections.text: Old installation remains: remove/disable obsolete app installation according to tenant policy and refresh OpsKnight discovery. War rooms fail after package update: confirm optional RSC permissions were included and consented in the target team.
